Description: In Helen Dauer’s room, Tony Dauer looks through the pocket watch and the box with a name on it, and talks with his mother Helen about etiquette, Eve Dauer, and the clue that he saw an “acquaintance.”
Location: Helen Dauer's room（Helen's room）
Key Information:
  - Distantly, piano music continues as ambient background sound.
  - Helen asks Tony how she looks; Tony brushes it off with “Great,” and Helen sees through that he didn’t really look.
  - Helen sternly orders Tony to put the pocket watch back, emphasizing his “dirty little hands” will leave fingerprints.
  - Tony says “He’s old anyway, he definitely won’t notice,” implying the watch belongs to an elderly man or will be checked by an elderly man.
  - Helen says she spent a lot of money on this and says she hopes the other party will be satisfied.
  - Tony notices a name written on the box and asks his mother; Helen says she doesn’t know and again orders him to put the watch back.
  - Tony complains Helen isn’t as harsh on Eve Dauer as she is on him; Helen says Eve is “a capable woman” and tells Tony to learn from her.
  - Tony tries to keep commenting on Eve but Helen cuts him off and tells them to go downstairs, reminding Tony to be polite to the hosts.
  - Tony says he’ll come down later because he thinks he just saw an acquaintance.
  - Helen reminds Tony not to cause trouble.
Characters:
  [Tony Dauer（Tony Dauer）] Person No. 4, Helen Dauer’s son.
    · Looks at the pocket watch in his mother’s room and asks about the name written on the box.
    · Assumes the owner is old and won’t notice fingerprints, showing a rash and disrespectful attitude.
    · Mentions he seems to have seen an acquaintance, so he decides to go downstairs later.
  [Helen Dauer（Helen Dauer）] Person No. 9, Tony Dauer’s mother.
    · Orders Tony to put the pocket watch back immediately to avoid fingerprints.
    · Says she spent a lot of money on something and hopes the other party will be satisfied.
    · Acknowledges Eve Dauer’s capability and tells Tony to be polite to the hosts and not cause trouble.
